title: Malta Year 8 Math Chapter 10 — Circles Practice
question: 15 circle questions, each with a picture: 5 Easy, 5 Medium, 5 Hard.
intro:
**Three levels:**

- Easy: radius and diameter, name a part, one formula
- Medium: circumference from the radius, area from the radius or the diameter, a quarter circle
- Hard: semicircles, a wheel turning, a fence, the most pizza

**Answers:** use \(\pi \approx 3.14\) and type the number only (no units).

questions.title: Round mirror
questions.prompt:
A round mirror has radius 12 cm.

Find its diameter.
questions.figure_alt: A round mirror with radius 12 cm drawn from the centre; the diameter across is the question mark.
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} d &= 2r \\ &= 2\times12 \\ &= \boxed{24} \end{aligned}\]

\(6\) halves the radius; the diameter is **double**.

questions.title: Dartboard
questions.prompt:
A dartboard has diameter 46 cm.

Find its radius.
questions.figure_alt: A dartboard with diameter 46 cm across; the radius from the centre is the question mark.
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} r &= d\div2 \\ &= 46\div2 \\ &= \boxed{23} \end{aligned}\]

\(92\) doubles; from the diameter, **halve**.

questions.title: Name the part
questions.prompt: What is the name of the blue line?
questions.figure_alt: A circle with one straight line from edge to edge that does not pass through the centre, drawn in blue.
questions.solution:
It goes from edge to edge but misses the centre:

\[\boxed{\text{chord}}\]

A diameter would go **through** the centre; a radius starts at the centre; a tangent stays outside and touches once.

questions.title: Round biscuit
questions.prompt:
A round biscuit has diameter 6 cm.

Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\).

Find its circumference.
questions.figure_alt: A round biscuit 6 cm across, rolled out into a line a bit more than 3 diameters long.
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} C &= \pi d \\ &= 3.14\times6 \\ &= \boxed{18.84} \end{aligned}\]

\(28.26\) is the area \(\pi r^2\), not the distance round.

questions.title: Flower bed
questions.prompt:
A round flower bed has radius 10 m.

Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\).

Find its area.
questions.figure_alt: A round flower bed with radius 10 m; its area is the question mark.
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} A &= \pi r^2 \\ &= 3.14\times10\times10 \\ &= 3.14\times100 \\ &= \boxed{314} \end{aligned}\]

\(62.8\) is the circumference \(2\pi r\).

questions.title: CD
questions.prompt:
A CD has radius 6 cm.

Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\).

Find its circumference.
questions.figure_alt: A CD with radius 6 cm, rolled out into a line; the length is the question mark.
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} d &= 2\times6 \\ &= 12 \\ C &= 3.14\times12 \\ &= \boxed{37.68} \end{aligned}\]

\(18.84\) forgets to double the radius.

questions.title: Placemat
questions.prompt:
A round placemat has radius 9 cm.

Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\).

Find its area.
questions.figure_alt: A round placemat with rings, radius 9 cm; its area is the question mark.

questions.title: Drum
questions.prompt:
The top of a drum is a circle with diameter 24 cm.

Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\).

Find its area.
questions.figure_alt: The round top of a drum with diameter 24 cm across; its area is the question mark.
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} r &= 24\div2 \\ &= 12 \\ r^2 &= 144 \\ A &= 3.14\times144 \\ &= \boxed{452.16} \end{aligned}\]

\(1808.64\) uses the diameter: \(24\times24\) is 4 times too big.

questions.title: Pond
questions.prompt:
The distance round a round pond is 31.4 m.

Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\).

Find its diameter.
questions.figure_alt: A round pond rolled out into a line 31.4 m long; its diameter is the question mark.
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} C &= \pi d \\ 31.4 &= 3.14\times d \\ d &= 31.4\div3.14 \\ &= \boxed{10} \end{aligned}\]

\(98.596\) multiplies by 3.14; to go back from \(C\) to \(d\), **divide**.

questions.title: Quarter-circle tile
questions.prompt:
A floor tile is a quarter circle with radius 10 cm.

Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\).

Find its area.
questions.figure_alt: A quarter circle with radius 10 cm along its straight edge and a right angle at the corner; its area is the question mark.
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} \pi r^2 &= 3.14\times100 \\ &= 314 \\ 314\div4 &= \boxed{78.5} \end{aligned}\]

\(314\) is the whole circle; a quarter circle is \(314\div4\).

questions.title: Semicircle perimeter
questions.prompt:
A window is a semicircle with diameter 20 cm.

Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\).

Find its perimeter (the curved edge plus the straight edge).
questions.figure_alt: A semicircle window with a 20 cm straight edge; the curved edge and the straight edge are both marked.
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} \pi d &= 3.14\times20 \\ &= 62.8 \\ 62.8\div2 &= 31.4 \\ 31.4 + 20 &= \boxed{51.4} \end{aligned}\]

\(31.4\) is only the curved edge; add the straight edge, 20 cm.

questions.title: Wheelchair wheel
questions.prompt:
A wheelchair wheel has diameter 0.6 m.

It turns 10 times.

Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\).

How far does it go?
questions.figure_alt: A wheel of diameter 0.6 m on the ground; an arrow shows 10 turns; the distance is the question mark.
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} C &= 3.14\times0.6 \\ &= 1.884 \\ 1.884\times10 &= \boxed{18.84} \end{aligned}\]

\(1.884\) is one turn only; 10 turns go 10 circumferences.

questions.title: Fountain fence
questions.prompt:
A round fountain has radius 7 m.

A fence goes once round its edge.

Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\).

How long is the fence?
questions.figure_alt: A round fountain with radius 7 m on square paving and a dashed fence round its edge; the length is the question mark.
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} d &= 2\times7 \\ &= 14 \\ C &= 3.14\times14 \\ &= \boxed{43.96} \end{aligned}\]

\(153.86\) is the area of the water; a fence goes **round**.

questions.title: Most pizza
questions.prompt:
Which offer gives the most pizza (the biggest total area)?

Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\).
questions.figure_alt: Four offers drawn to scale: A two 15 cm pizzas, B one 30 cm pizza, C three 10 cm pizzas, D four 12 cm pizzas.
questions.solution:
Area of one pizza: radius = half the diameter, then \(3.14\times r^2\).

- A: \(2\times3.14\times7.5^2 = 353.25\)
- B: \(1\times3.14\times15^2 = 706.5\)
- C: \(3\times3.14\times5^2 = 235.5\)
- D: \(4\times3.14\times6^2 = 452.16\)

\[\boxed{\text{B: one pizza of 30 cm}}\]

Doubling the diameter makes the area **4 times** as big, so one 30 cm pizza beats two 15 cm pizzas.

questions.title: Semicircle lawn
questions.prompt:
A lawn is a semicircle with radius 6 m.

Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\).

Find its area.
questions.figure_alt: A semicircle lawn with radius 6 m; its area is the question mark.
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} \pi r^2 &= 3.14\times36 \\ &= 113.04 \\ 113.04\div2 &= \boxed{56.52} \end{aligned}\]

\(113.04\) is the whole circle; a semicircle is half.

takeaway:
- \(d = 2r\) and \(r = d\div2\).
- Distance round: \(C = \pi d\).
- Space inside: \(A = \pi r^2\), with the **radius**.
- A semicircle's perimeter adds the straight edge.
